title: Nikon Advanced Microscopy - Confocal Reflection Label-Free Imaging
author: Akihiro Suto

steps.title: Prepare Sample and Initial Experiment
steps.instruction: Place the sample onto the microscope stage and initialize the experiment in AX Confocal software.

substeps.instruction: Add an experiment on the AX Confocal
Add fluorophores present in sample and press finish

steps.title: Configure Reflected Channel in Expert Mode
steps.instruction: Enter Expert Mode in the experiment configuration to add and define a reflected acquisition channel.

substeps.instruction: Enter Expert Mode in experiment configuration
Add an extra channel to the experiment and select the reflected acquisition toggle
Rename the channel and apply a false color if desired

steps.title: Assign Detector for Reflected Channel
steps.instruction: Reassign the reflected channel to a tunable GaAsPs detector in position 2 or 3.

substeps.instruction: Cut the connection from the connected channel to the 4th detector by clicking on the line
Drag and drop from the red box to reconnect the channel to GaAsP detector 2 or 3

steps.title: Optimize Acquisition Settings
steps.instruction: Configure the frame pass and filter range for the reflected channel.

substeps.instruction: Set the reflected channel to be imaged on a separate pass (frame pass)
Extend the variable filter range to cover the laser excitation for the reflected channel

steps.title: Adjust Optical Setup
steps.instruction: Access the expert setup to modify the dichroic mirror and scan area.

substeps.instruction: Open experiment setup in expert mode and click on the first dichroic mirror
Move the scan area away from the center of the field of view

steps.title: Calibrate Signal Intensity
steps.instruction: Gradually adjust gain and laser power to visualize the reflected channel without overexposing the detector.

substeps.instruction: Start with low gain and laser power
Slowly increase gain and laser power until the reflected channel is visualized
Ensure laser power remains very low to avoid overexposing the PMT
